whatIsIt.eli5: YOLO26's body-point head. It also learns how sure it is about each point while training.
whatIsIt.simple: Like the Pose head, with one-to-many and one-to-one copies and no DFL. The keypoint branch first makes shared features, then one 1×1 Conv gives the points and (only in training) another gives an uncertainty for each point. A tiny flow network (RealNVP) is used by the RLE loss in training.
whatIsIt.engineer: cv4 = Conv3×3 → Conv3×3 (c4 = max(ch0/4, K·(D+2))); cv4_kpts Conv2d(c4, K·D); cv4_sigma Conv2d(c4, 2K) (training); flow_model RealNVP (training, RLE).

whyExists.eli5: Knowing how sure it is helps the model learn points better.
whyExists.simple: Residual Log-Likelihood Estimation models the error of each keypoint as a learned distribution, which Ultralytics says improves keypoint accuracy.
whyExists.engineer: RLE (Li et al., 2021) with a normalising flow over residuals; sigma/flow are training-only.

eli5: Guess each point; while learning, also guess how sure.
simple: Box and class branches as usual (both copies).
cv4_kpts predicts x, y, visibility for each keypoint.
Training only: cv4_sigma predicts an uncertainty per keypoint; RealNVP turns it into a likelihood for the loss.
engineer: Inference outputs: boxes, scores, kpts [K·D, A]; kpts_sigma only when training.

example.eli5: For people: 17 points × 3 numbers = 51 numbers per guess.
